utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic, and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. First of all, as a matter of courtesy I should explain the reason for our delay in taking the Bench is that we were on the other side of the door discussing a number of procedural matters relative to this trial. May we have the appearances for the today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Office of the Prosecutor, Gerard Dobbyn with Belinda Pidwell and Crispian Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, Aleksandar Aleksic, and Jason Antley for the Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the witness returns to the stand, do we correctly understand that the Defence has something to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we were invited and instructed by the Trial Chamber to give our position on the latest amendment of -- motion to amend the 65 ter list in relation to Witness ST-197. So I would make that submission and short explanation, and I will -- I will speak in Serbian, Your Honours. [Interpretation] Your Honours, in support of what I said yesterday in my address to the Honourable Trial Chamber, we have before us yet another document that we have to state your position on. We received an amendment for the 65 ter list for Witness ST-197, scheduled to testify next week. We received it yesterday. Two new topics are now contained in the 65 ter list, and we agree with the Prosecution that they're relevant for this case, but we had not been aware of the fact that this witness would be testifying about that, although the witness was interviewed as early as in April 2010 and again in August, in early August, again 2010. Now, that makes me wonder whether the Prosecution was not in a position to announce in April or in May that there was a possibility the witness might be testifying about those issues. Rule 126 bis gives the Defence 14 days to respond to motions of this kind filed by the Prosecution, Your Honours. Again, as they did yesterday, the Prosecution asked us to state our position in 24 hours. I absolutely understand the Trial Chamber's reasons. The witness is at the door, at the courtroom door, but this practice implemented by the Prosecution seeking amendments to the 65 ter list immediately before the witness is about to take the stand is, in my opinion, entirely inappropriate, and let me explain why I think that it is so. In this case the Defence agrees with the Prosecution that it is absolutely relevant to include the issues in the testimony of Witness ST-197, and this witness really probably might assist us to clarify some of the issues at issue here, and if I had enough time to go through all the documents, I perhaps would not be opposing the amendment of the 65 ter list. But in a situation like this when I am facing a fait accompli, when I don't have enough time to analyse the documents and the witness -- witness's statement, I have to oppose this amendment of the 65 ter list. This goes for the case of this witness and perhaps also for the case of -- that we discussed yesterday. Yesterday, my learned friend Mr. Dobbyn stated that in the course of the disclosure they were disclosing to us materials relevant to the testimony of the witnesses that were included in the witness list at a later stage. I claim that it is only partly true. Most of the disclosure that we received contain documents for the witnesses who are about to take the stand. Let me give you an example. Now we're talking about Witness ST-197. From the 16th of August, Your Honours, until yesterday, so it's 14 days, we received a total of seven batches of documents, which means that on the average every other day we received a batch of documents. Yesterday, on the 1st of September, we received batch 138 which supporting materials pertaining to Witness ST-197, who is about to take the stand. He's due to testify on Monday. A week ago, we received by way of disclosure video material lasting longer of -- longer than four hours. That's part of batch 136. And the quality of the audio recording was very bad, which means that it takes us much more time to actually go through it, to listen to it. Yesterday, we received a total of nine documents pertaining to this witness totaling 687 pages of documents, transcripts, and photographs. At first glance at least 50 per cent of those are very relevant and call for serious analysis, and I claim here and now that despite all of our preparations we will be unable to get ready for the witness, for his cross-examination. The Trial Chamber knows that the Defence is obliged to state its position on the motion pertaining to 92 bis witnesses. We will agree to it. We are also seeking to find a solution with the Prosecution for the exhumations. We are preparing the cross-examination of witnesses who come here day by day, and we have to say aside this urgent business in order to address urgently the motions for the amendment of 65 ter lists, the supporting materials, additional materials, and the deluge of documents that hit us every 24 hours. I would like to assure you, Your Honours, that the Defence is unable to meet those demands. I simply do not know how this situation can be resolved, and the only solution that I see is for the trial to be adjourned for a few days. It's an unpopular measure, I know, but the Prosecution should be given a certain deadline to deal with the 20 witnesses from the original list, to give us any motions for the amendment of the 65 ter lists and all the documents that they might have pertaining to those witnesses, and then we can continue. I would like to notify the Trial Chamber about yet another fact which will become a hot topic quite soon. It's the Prosecution military expert. I don't have any information, but common sense tells me that we will be receiving a new report from that expert, modified to be in line with the documents obtained in the action to capture Ratko Mladic. I have information from other cases tried before this Tribunal that there are about 150 hours of audio and video recordings and an additional expert report, expert analysis, carried out by the minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia containing several hundreds of pages, and this material has already been disclosed in other cases. Not in this case, however. And now I can share this with you: This will force us to seek an adjournment of the proceedings in order to be able to analyse the documents and to prepare for the cross-examination of the Prosecution expert. Your Honours, by way of conclusion, the gist of it is this: Yesterday I made a submission. I explained the position of the Defence, and today, the very same day as I was drafting the Defence submission, we kept receiving a huge amount of documents and new motions to amend the 65 ter list. So I really consider that the Prosecution has not taken the Defence demand seriously, because I cannot see any other justification or explanation. I'm really sorry that I'm taking up so much of your time, Your Honours, but this is a serious issue, because it really affects the ability of the Defence to prepare for the trial. Thank you very much, and I do apologise once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let me just add to what Mr. Zecevic has said. We fully subscribe to everything he has said, and this is a joint position of the Defence teams of Stanisic and Zupljanin. As far as Witness ST-197 is concerned, the modification of his evidence at the last minute, at the eleventh hour makes it impossible for us to cross-examine him next week. It's not only about the amount of the material. It is video footage and documents that we did not take into consideration when we were preparing our cross-examination. When the Defence prepares to cross-examine, they take into account the material disclosed and stays within the scope of the Prosecution summary of witness evidence. With this substantial expansion of this scope, the Defence is no longer able to prepare in time. I don't know any of the people who are to be seen on this video footage. I have to send investigators to check this on the ground, to examine this. Otherwise, we cannot fully prepare to cross-examine the witness. Therefore, if the Trial Chamber is considering the possibility to expand the testimony of Witness ST-197, I would like to suggest that we move his evidence to the week beginning with the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, there are two related but separate issues. One is the expanded evidence -- expanded testimony, as you have described it, but more importantly, and what I understand to be common to yourself and Mr. Zecevic, is the general problem about late disclosure, and in that context I would ask you -- I suppose I should have asked Mr. Zecevic, but it's a common question, and that is the implied application that you are -- would make for an adjournment. How much time would your application -- how much time would you require according to any application that you have indicated you may be forced to make in order to deal with -- with this new material which was just recently disclosed? It's information which the Chamber -- would be useful to the Chamber in making its decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe, as Mr. Zecevic has said and after consulting him, that in order to really prepare we would need two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the OTP -- does the OTP have any comments on the -- on the reply which had been -- replies which have been articulated by counsel for the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, our view is that at this present time we have two witnesses who are backed up, waiting to come into court. The witness in question is due to come next week. We feel that this would be better dealt with after these two witnesses have been seen. We're taking up valuable court time to argue this matter, delaying the witnesses that we already have here waiting in The Hague. However, I understand that they've now asked -- they are seeking an adjournment of Witness ST-197, so if you would like to hear our specific submissions on what they've said, then, yes, we will do that now. Sorry, or alternatively at the end of the day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps it may be more -- I was going to say, perhaps it may be more efficient to leave it to the end of the day, because I realise we have a witness outside the door who is waiting to continue his testimony. Of course, we have learned from bitter experience that trying fit these things at the end of the day we find ourselves pressed for time and the time for adjournment is upon us, but perhaps we can continue with the witness and counsel can consult during the break, and we can decide when would be the most efficient time to deal with this. Could the usher have the witness ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn, without -- before we -- as I said, we're going to return to the broader issues which have been raised by Defence counsels' submissions, but in terms of 197 specifically, the matter of this new material, it isn't clear to us from the motion as to, (A) when this information came to the notice of the Prosecution; and (B), when it was disclosed to the Defence. Could you assist us with that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I'm taking this information from the motion that the new information became available to the Prosecution upon interviewing the witness first on the 12th of March of 2010 and again on the 6th of August, 2010, and the statements or interview transcripts from those meetings with the witness were then disclosed to the Defence on 12th of March -- excuse me. I have that -- sorry. One second, Your Honours. On the 15th of April and the 10th of August, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn, this is general information that is indeed in the motion, but what we would like to know is a little bit more precise. There are more or less three issues of new material. At what time did you get each of them, and at what time did you disclose? At what moment did you disclose each of them?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: By the new material, Your Honours, just to be clear, I wonder is this the -- the matter that was raised by my learned colleague about the most recent disclosure batch that went out yesterday? I'm not quite -- I'm not understanding what you mean by the "new material."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: From the top of my head, there is the meeting between the witness and Mr. Zupljanin. There is the new material on the Vlasic Mountain -- Vlasic Mountain incident, and the new material on the resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness had previously been interviewed about Vlasic Mountain, and that was contained in his original 65 ter summary that he would be testifying about Vlasic Mountain. Now, the -- there is one line added, I see, to the motion concerning Vlasic Mountain, and I -- in my submission, Your Honour, that can really be inferred into the original 65 ter summary. It's -- it's clarifying the specifics about what he would be testifying about Vlasic Mountain. It's really just making it clear. It's not a new matter in that respect. Now, with regards to the -- the issue of resubordination, again, Your Honours, I -- I have to say on that point I would need to check further. I don't know. I don't have that information off the top of my head at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: About the meeting between the witness and Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: That's the other matter which I'd also need to check on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, good afternoon to you. We apologise that the continuation of your testimony has been delayed, but the nature of trials is that in addition to receiving testimony, invariably courts have procedural matters with which to deal, and some of it would have continued after you were escorted back to the stand. So I remind you you're still on your oath, and I would invite Mr. Krgovic to resume his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krejic, good afternoon. Let us pick up where we left off yesterday. I started a line of questioning yesterday, but then we had to cut it short because we had to adjourn for the day, but let me repeat. Let me recap. When the Prosecutor asked you a question you said that on that day when all of you went to the scene, General Subotic and other people who were present at the meeting, that Mr. Zupljanin was not with you.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zupljanin was not at the site on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 23rd of August, when you went to the site together with your colleague Mr. Veleusic, Mr. Zupljanin was not at Koricanske Stijene, at the site on that occasion either, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't there on that occasion either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on that day, the 23rd, you spoke with Mr. Zupljanin at least twice, at first time when you called him and when he instructed you to go to the site, and the second time when you called him upon your return from the site to inform him about what you had found there.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And both times he was in Banja Luka when you called him on the phone, either in the security services centre or you used the dedicated line.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the next day, the 24th, when the meeting took place at the security services centre, there was no visit to the site. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all the microphones that are not in use be kindly switched off.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we didn't go to the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And after the meeting, all the participants went their own way. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And on that day, Mr. Zupljanin did not go to Koricanske Stijene, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You were the chief of the public security station in Knezevo up until the 31st of August, if I understood you correctly. I'm talking about 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In that period between the 24th, when the meeting took place, and the last meeting after which you no longer were at the post in the public security station in Knezevo, Stojan Zupljanin never came to Vakuf or Knezevo and Koricanske Stijene, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because if you wanted to go to Koricanske Stijene, you had to pass through Knezevo. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the only route. And I think that he would have stopped by to see me, because we were on such terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And it was usual practice that any visits by the chief or any other high-ranking officials were to be announced either to you or to the president of the Executive Board or the president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was usual practice. Chief Zupljanin had a lot of respect for his subordinates, and if he had come to Knezevo on any kind of business he would have come to see me and I would have known that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I have a little doubt in this respect due to what the witness showed us on the geographical map of the municipality. Mr. Witness, Koricanske Stijene, is that within the borders of the municipality or just past the borders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the war and indeed at the time when the incidents we're talking about occurred at Koricanske Stijene, Koricanske Stijene were not part of the municipality of Knezevo. Koricanske Stijene, this is located as you are about -- as you are about to leave the municipality of Knezevo in the direction of Travnik. The distance from the Municipal Boarder is about 2 to 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's -- that's how you -- you indicated it on the map that was shown to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And in light of the fact that this area was controlled by the Republika Srpska forces, for all intents and purposes this unit that you mentioned that had been resubordinated to the army was deployed in that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but further down from Koricanske Stijene, some 4 to 5 kilometres further on, into the depth of the municipality of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, in talks with the people in the municipality and the Executive Board in those days and after that, did you receive any information that Stojan Zupljanin had visited the area of Koricanske Stijene in that period while the investigation was going on and so on?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. I never received any such information either through official or unofficial channels to the effect that Chief Zupljanin had been in the area, in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, the Prosecutor also asked you about a survivor, the one that you took to Banja Luka. You described how that transpired, and you told us that Mr. Zupljanin had told you -- well, the interpretation was a bit unclear, that you were responsible, that you were to guarantee his safety. Did Mr. Zupljanin tell you that you had to guarantee personally that this man would reach Banja Luka safe and sound?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that he would reach Banja Luka safe and sound, and that I would be held responsible for any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you definitely know that there was high security risk for the survivors of the massacre and that either perpetrators or people who wanted to solidarise with them might want to harm them and that their security and safety were indeed at risk; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of the municipality of Knezevo there were no perpetrators of the massacre. And as for the rest of the population, the troops and the Republika Srpska police, they were not a threat to those people. They didn't threaten their lives or threaten them in any other way. Quite the opposite. They were treated humanely right from the time when they were found until they were handed over to the responsible authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstand me, but I'm -- I was referring to the time period when you took them over until their hand-over to the Red Cross and their stay in the hospital in Banja Luka. Were there any safety concerns about those people, that their lives might be in danger?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right here. That's why I, although I did not have any suspicions as to Chief Zupljanin's intentions, I wanted to meet Chief Zupljanin, and I asked him what would happen to that man. I wanted to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And disclosing the identity and the number of survivors of the massacre to the public would put them at risk and would jeopardise the investigation. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I suppose that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And of course if the intention was for those people to be transferred from the territory of Republika Srpska to the territory controlled by the federation safely, it was unwise to -- to make public the -- their identity, number, and route they would take, their movements. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Just a correction for the transcript. I may have misspoken, but when we talked about the territory, the border with the municipality of Knezevo, it was controlled by the Republika Srpska Army, wasn't it? The Koricanske Stijene. This is the area where your unit was.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was controlled by the Republika Srpska Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to revisit another topic. When you spoke about the meeting at which Mr. Zupljanin read out the dispatch, the wire that he claimed had been sent by Mr. Karadzic, you thought that in essence Mr. Zupljanin was the author of the document and that he was exploiting it, exploiting the authority of President Karadzic to gain control over Simo Drljaca. You testified to that effect before the court in Sarajevo. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not 100 per cent certain that that is the case, but I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to a topic that is not directly related to this line of questioning. When you spoke about the ethnic composition of the municipality of Knezevo, you mentioned a certain number of Croat villages that were marked as such in an area. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And when the conflict broke out when inter-ethnic tensions appeared in Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was an agreement in place for the villages that were bordering with the Croat areas should develop ties with those areas that were controlled by the Croat forces. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the first multi-party elections, when the HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union had it's deputies in the Knezevo Municipal Assembly, we and the deputies of the SDA and of the SDS agreed, before the conflict broke out, that an approval should be granted to them to establish their own municipality in the area which were -- which was 100 per cent Croatian. It was a compact area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, did this really happen, or was it just in theory?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, as the Assembly in which the SDS had more than half of deputies, we gave our approval, but in addition to the municipal approval, they had to get the approval of the Assembly of the republic, and the war broke out and put a stop to all those activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, I showed you a video-tape yesterday, and I asked you to identify some persons. Now I would like you to look at the same video, and I would like you to identify some things that can be seen in the recording.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we play Prosecution Exhibit 1563.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's the video-clip that you saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you continue, because we can't see this very clearly. [In English] Okay. Stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krejic, this is the crime scene technician's equipment, kit. Based on my knowledge of forensic procedures, this is the kit used for identification, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What exactly are we talking about, the green suitcase or the piece of cloth that he's holding in his hand or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The green suitcase, and the other thing is a camera, still photography camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to check -- stop here, please. Could you please rewind a little bit. [In English] Stop now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see what this man has at his left hip?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a still camera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I think we did establish this yesterday, so there's no reason to go into this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I simply wanted to use a more qualified witness to make sure we have it right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Krejic, yesterday I asked you, you may recall, about the initial reports about possible perpetrators of the crime. Now I would like to show you a document. It's P676. It's at tab 5 in Stanisic Defence binder. Sir, this is a report from the 1st Krajina Corps Command to the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army. The date is the 22nd of August, 1992. I would like you to look at item number 4. It's down at the bottom of the page. It says: "When the refugee columns were escorted across Mount Vlasic ..." Now we need to move to page 2 of this document. In the Serbian version. "... to Travnik, a group of police officers from Prijedor and Sanski Most took out about 100 Muslims, killed them in various ways and threw their bodies into a ravine." Have you seen this document before, perhaps during your testimony at some trial or during your proofing sessions with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't think so. I don't think I've seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this completes my cross-examination of this witness. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to clear up one matter that I believe would be of assistance to all of us, including the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P -- P1572 is the document I would need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you remember the photograph you marked yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With number 2, you marked the location where you saw the larger group of bodies when you first came to the site with that colleague from the public security station Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose there were some bodies outside this circle, down below in the gorge.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Most of the bodies were somewhere halfway down the cliff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, could you mark where the other bodies at the bottom of the gorge were?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May we have the assistance of the usher for markings on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a problem here. You can't see the bottom of the gorge on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Uh-huh. So the bottom of the photograph is not the bottom of the canyon?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, can you mark in approximately, roughly, all the places where there were bodies, as far as you can see on this photo.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, let me make one thing clear. All this terrain gravitating towards the circle is the side of the canyon on Travnik territory, whereas this part towards me is Knezevo territory. You can't see the bottom of the canyon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This line you've just drawn in red, does it mark how the bodies were lying?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there were some bodies below as well where you can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow to show what you mean by "further down."

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this red line represents the bodies that were in that part of the canyon, and below them were more bodies at the very bottom of the canyon. Is that what the photograph is showing?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they didn't go to the bottom of the canyon. The distance between the line and the bottom of the canyon is approximately the same as the distance between the line and the road, and the bodies were not close to the very bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you mark this line and the arrow with a number 3.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, what is the difference in altitude between the road where you were standing and this first group of bodies that you marked with a circle on this photograph marked with 2?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty to 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it's very steep, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Extremely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So we could say that these bodies below marked with a line and number 3 were 50 metres down roughly. Does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suggest that this document be admitted, if there is no objection, with the additional marking and with his clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D363, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, at the very beginning of your evidence you said you were a teacher of national defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my occupation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose you graduated from the faculty of national defence.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the University of Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose, then, you are familiar with the fundamental regulations governing national defence and social self-protection.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These regulations are, in fact, the foundation for the subject called national defence at your school, at the faculty.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'll read out to you and I'll show you document 1D04-2409. It's the instruction on the use of Territorial Defence issued by the Federal Secretariat for National Defence. It was published in Belgrade by the Military Publishing Institute in 1977.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown page 4 in Serbian. The English page is the one we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just check which tab number this is on the list of documents we received from Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this instruction? Do you know this document? I know it's not so easy to view it on the screen, but I have a hard copy, if you wish. You can leaf through it, refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That won't be necessary. It's an instruction, just any other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the Federal Secretariat for National Defence issued such instructions to the forces of the Yugoslav People's Army, and of course you are familiar with them.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And there were dozens of them.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were, but I suppose there were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I need your comment on two points contained in the general provisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 17 in Serbian in e-court, and I suppose it could be page 12 in English, but I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't want you to think that I'm trying to take something out of context, so I would like you to look at the full document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher could help me pass this document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For you it's pages 11 and 12. This is chapter 1, and the heading is "General Provisions." You see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And paragraph 4 stipulates who is a member of the armed forces by law. It says: "The armed forces are a unified armed force within the system of national defence ... any citizen participating in the resistance against the aggressor either by taking arms or any other way shall be considered a member of the armed forces." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This paragraph 4 is in full conformity with all regulations that governed at the time the national defence and social self-protection, the subject in which you -- the subject which you read at university?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say it was the basic postulate you mean it was the foundation on which the entire system rested?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the entire system rested on it, and it defined the armed forces, what they meant, what they consisted of in the SFRY, the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show page 18 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And for you it would be page 13. It's paragraph 6 that straddles another page. It deals with the Territorial Defence. I'm interested in the last two paragraphs of this para 6. It says: "The Territorial Defence is equipment to carry out, either with the JNA units or independently, combat operations in the temporarily occupied territory along the front line and in its own rear." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I suppose this is sufficiently well explained in English. I don't think it needs further explanation. And the last point that interests me most is this: "In the case of immediate threat of war and during wartime, the police forms a part of the Territorial Defence and is engaged in carrying out certain combat and security tasks." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When it says "the police," in Serbian "milicija," that's the old name for the police, the members of the Ministry of the Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This was also one of the basic postulates in the general design of the national defence and social self-protection system?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in the event of immediate threat of war or an ongoing war, according to the basic postulates of the system of national defence, the police became part of the Territorial Defence force, and it was engaged in combat, security, and other tasks. However, whenever they are carrying out tasks of this kind, members of the police, members of the MUP, are under the command of a military unit.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I wonder if you could assist us with a brief explanation. I think we all understand the term "combat tasks." These are tasks carried out in the course of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Other tasks are also somehow related to combat operations or military actions, but they are not direct combat.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could describe it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us what security tasks means?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this context as it is written here, I understand security tasks to mean certain security tasks in the area of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the time, Your Honour. I suppose it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. I was just waiting for a convenient point. I know we started a little late, so I -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, as a result of some discussions over the break, I'm just asking for -- that we finish with the witnesses half an hour early tonight in order to discuss the issues that have come up so far. Sorry, that we be given half an hour before the close to discuss those issues. Also, I believe there will be some further ongoing discussions over the next break about issues that we're hoping to resolve with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So noted, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, sorry, one other matter I'd like to add for the record, that Matthew Olmsted has joined the Prosecution in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Mr. Krejic, when we were discussing this, you mentioned security tasks and other tasks. I think you testified yesterday that on the day when you went for the first time to the crime scene at Koricanske Stijene, you spoke with the members of the public security station Knezevo, who were at that moment deployed -- or, rather, resubordinated to the military unit in a locality about 5 kilometres away from the scene. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this unit of yours, I saw it somewhere in one of your previous statements, had 25 members of the public security station Knezevo, which was resubordinated to some Tactical Group that was carrying out some military operations in that area.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: They were resubordinated to that military unit, but their task, the task of that unit, was, in fact, to secure the road, the Travnik-Knezevo road, at that time.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, their task was indeed to secure that road but not securing that road internally. That road passed through the zone of separation between the Army of Republika Srpska and the Croatian Defence Council, so that this unit was carrying out combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned in your answer to the previous question, when you mentioned, I think, the area of responsibility of a military unit, if I understand this correctly, the area of responsibility of a military unit is not just the territory where combat operations are taking place, but it is the entire territory occupied by that military unit or covered by that military unit.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the area of the 22nd Brigade, which was on the Vlasic plateau, went from Karanovac, which is a suburb of Banja Luka, up to the front line, and that covers a depth behind the lines of about 70 or 80 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said 70 to 80 kilometres, right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that specific case it was 70 to 80 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 10236, para 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show you the same map shown to you by my learned friend Mr. Dobbyn, just to look at the geography without accepting the picture presented on that map. I just want you to delineate on the map the area that was the area of responsibility of the 22nd Krajina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number of the 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 10236.13. I suppose it has a P number now, but, I'm sorry, I can't find it now. If you give me a minute. Could we zoom in a bit for the witness. We don't need the upper part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You've seen this map before. It shows the territory of Skender Vakuf and Knezevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, could you mark on this map what exactly was the territory the area of responsibility of the 22nd Krajina Brigade.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just the 22nd Brigade, it's not Krajina Brigade. Apart from the entire territory of Knezevo municipality, the responsibility of the 22nd Brigade stretched onto a great part of the Celinac municipality, which is not drawn here, and the entire territory of Kotor Varos Municipality. This is it. One part of Travnik municipality and the entire territory of Knezevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So what you just delineated in red is the area of responsibility of the 22nd Brigade that is seen on this map, but in addition to this, it also covered the area up to Karanovac, which is almost a suburb of Banja Luka, that is to say 70 to 80 per cent -- sorry, 70 to 80 kilometres behind the lines.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark this with 1 as the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D364, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: While we are still on this subject, and I believe it may be also of assistance to the Trial Chamber and to all of us if I show you another document -- or, rather, I'll ask you a question first. At what point did the 22nd Brigade take control of the Knezevo municipality -- or, rather, the territory that was covered by the public security of -- station of Knezevo?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This used to be called the 122nd Brigade of the JNA, and it came to Knezevo municipality from Slavonia, which is currently the Republic of Croatia, after the so-called Vance Plan was adopted. That is when the JNA units left Croatia, and sometime in March 1992 they were stationed in Knezevo municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. The commander of this unit was Colonel Bosko Peulic. I don't know if he was yet a colonel at that time.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't, but he was the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When that unit under his command took position on this territory, they took over all the functions of the civilian authorities in that municipality.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not take over, but they sought to, and that was a constant source of strife between the command of the brigade and Peulic and the leadership of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When we interviewed you in the presence of the Prosecutor, I believe you told me that when Peulic arrived, he acted like a conquistador. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were moments when it seemed exactly like that, metaphorically, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you used that metaphor, you meant to indicate that he acted autocratically, as untouchable.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the full sense of that word.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood your statements and your evidence correctly, the command headed by Peulic kept asking and insisting that they receive all sorts of materiel and supplies, and they wanted to have priority over everything else, every aspect of life in Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and they meddled with every aspect of normal life in Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that caused a lot of friction between the municipal authorities, including also you as chief of the public security station on one hand and that military unit on the other?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was the piggy in the middle between the political leadership and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document that relates to this issue. It's 1D04-2846. It's tab 18 in our binder of documents, and it's an instruction on civilian affairs in crisis areas, issued by the Federal Secretariat for National Defence, the Department of Civilian Defence, and it was signed by the Assistant Federal Secretary for National Defence, Major-General Milan Pujic, and the date is 25 November 1991. Did you maybe have occasion to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Today was the first time I saw it myself. This document deals with the conduct of civilian affairs in crisis areas, and it is intended for members of the armed forces. Can you confirm this? This document is meant for members of the armed forces on how to conduct civilian affairs in crisis areas.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in commands of JNA units and later the Army of Republika Srpska there was an organ for civilian affairs? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This says that this has the character of an instruction and needs to be applied in practice, adapted to the actual circumstances on the ground. Do you see that in the last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On this page 2, the first one was an explanation on the delivery of this instruction, and this speaks about the tasks of the organ for civilian affairs in JNA unit commands and the local command. Was a local command indeed established in Knezevo by the 22nd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had their own Knezevo command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here you see a list of tasks, basic tasks, and how the programmes should be adapted to the actual conditions and the areas of responsibility and jurisdiction. That's the third paragraph. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in essence this is a general document which allowed the commanders of some units in the area of responsibility -- in their area of responsibility and their civil affairs officers to adapt and modify those measures to bring them in line with the circumstances in the field. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like to see the next page, page 3. This -- well, these are specific tasks where the instruction itself is further elaborated, and under Roman numeral I it says: "Tasks from the area of state administration, legislative, judicial, and executive authority or government." And item 7 reads: "If the military command deems that the civilian authority no longer functions, the units' commands shall take measures and create conditions for the establishment and functioning of the organs of civilian government or civilian authorities." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to go to the next page. This pertains to the tasks in the sphere of security. And we will dwell on this for a while longer, because I think those affected the operation of the public security station where you severed as chief. You can see here the Roman numeral II, it says: "Tasks in the Sphere of Security." Item 1: "Assisting in the organisation of labour within the area of internal affairs." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any idea what this assisting in the organisation of labour in the sphere of internal affairs might refer to?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the only thing that I can think of is providing assistance to the organs of the interior in setting up operations in the recently liberated areas where there had been no organs of the interior present.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You can see item 6 here where it says: "Taking and implementation of investigative actions and submission of criminal complaints against perpetrators of crimes."

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These are the tasks that are within your purview under the Law on Internal Affairs. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that this creates a certain double chain of command in terms of powers or authority.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that in the interpretation is the chain of command, but I said duality in powers, which means that two organs, one an organ of the interior which has it's powers under the Law on Internal Affairs, and on the other hand you have military organs which, on the basis of this instruction, have the same powers in crisis areas. This is the duality that I had in mind when I asked my question, and probably you had the same in mind when you answered.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was the gist of my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see item 9: "Providing assistance for securing and performance of official tasks within the purview of other authorities." This is also one of the tasks under the Law on Internal Affairs, is it not, of the organs of the interior?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The same goes for item 9 where we're talking about security measures for buildings and other property and persons?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you mentioned item 9 in your previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I referred to item 10 where it says: "Participation in the organisation of tasks --" No. I do apologise. I'm sorry. In my previous question I actually invoked item 8, and now I'm talking about item 9, securing buildings, other property and persons.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's item 9, and we've dealt with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Item 10, it says: "Participation in organising tasks in the performance of the control and regulation of traffic on roads, controlling the movement and stay of foreign nationals in the border areas," and so on. These are also tasks that are in the purview of the organs of the interior?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 100 per cent. This is something that the minister of the interior does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In item 11, they are given powers to carry out administrative tasks pertaining to the purchase, carrying, and possession of weapons and ammunition, and they can issue licenses for that.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is strictly -- this had strictly been a power of the Ministry of the Interior, did these kind of administrative jobs?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 15, which reads: "Ensuring that appropriate repressive measures are taken against individuals and groups and enforcement of special powers and duties in security tasks (checking identity, summons, bringing in, remand, arrest, bringing into custody, searches, use of physical force and firearms, restricting the freedom of movement in an area, and isolation measures)." Pursuant to this item, the military organs have the powers that the organs of the interior did not have under the law; isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the organs of the interior do have these powers, all of them as far as I was able to read, and we can see that the military organs want to actually seize some of those powers, to appropriate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see in item 16 it says: "Providing assistance in ensuring the appropriate conditions for the functioning of the judicial organs, the penitentiary and correctional facilities and detention camps, and the control over the enforcement of the arrest and detention of detainees." The powers that under these instruction are given to the military organs are the powers that under the law of internal -- on internal affairs you, as members of the organs of the interior, did not have. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This -- these are tasks that are normally within the purview of the Justice Ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I know that the witness has not seen this document. I don't know what the Prosecution's position is, but in light of the fact that we've commented on this document in the course of the cross-examination, I would like to tender it. This is an official instruction, and it appears to me to be quite relevant for our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D365, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I think that I've neglected to tender document 1D04-2409. It's the document that I went through with the witness at the very beginning. It's at tab 17. It's the instruction on the use of the Territorial Defence, or perhaps if we could mark it for identification and then perhaps once I have -- once I have more time we can choose the relevant -- select just the relevant parts so that we don't tender the whole document. It's a voluminous document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes, that might be a good idea, but before we take any position on the matter, I just wish to ensure that these instructions were indeed in force in 1992. I note that they were dated 1977, if I'm not mistaken, and so -- I mean, if they were no longer in force, it would make little sense to consider admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The query I have is that although they are instructions, whether they did not form as a category of -- of something which should be part of a law library.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was exactly my -- my thinking, along these lines, Your Honours. This might be -- as far as the Defence is aware, these are the instructions which were valid at the -- which were in force in 1992. They -- they were prepared for the JNA troops, and as we can see, this 22nd was -- was -- was actually the JNA -- the JNA unit, and only after the creation of VRS it became the 122nd Brigade of the VRS. I agree with Your Honours that this could qualify as a part of the law library, but unfortunately, Your Honours, I received the document just this morning, so due to that I didn't have time to consult with my friends from the -- from the Prosecutor's side, and that is why I suggest we just MFI the document and then we will inform the Trial Chamber of what is the agreement between the parties about this document, whether we would admit it in its entirety into the law library or just the relevant parts under the -- the exhibit number which will be given as MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So for the time being we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would agree to that being added to the law library in entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we needn't -- so we rescind the order marking it for identification, and it would become part of the law library by whatever process that is achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure Mr. Dobbyn and myself will be very criticised and hated by our assistants who are working on this law library, because it was my understanding that they had just finished the updated version, but we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- we will proceed in accordance with Your Honour's ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But this begs the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This begs the question as to whether the most recent document that we admitted should also be a part of the law library. These also appear as being instructions by the old --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- federal --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is instruction is in the form of a book, and this other instructions which we admitted are in the form of a document, and therefore I cannot honestly say at this point whether it's -- it qualifies to be the part of law library, but I think -- I think for the time being maybe we can leave it as it is and then readdress the issue later if that -- if that is acceptable to the Trial Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So the document will be marked 1D366, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So I stand corrected. The document will not be exhibited, and this is the document 1D04-2409.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, in addition to graduating from the faculty of national defence and teaching national defence in school, at one point in late 1992, you actually headed a unit of the public security station in Knezevo which actually had been resubordinated in the Posavina theatre; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you are referring to my stint in Posavina, well, that was at the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it is a fact that the unit from Knezevo, together with you as the chief, was resubordinated to a military unit and was engaged in combat in the territory of the municipality of Odzak, if I'm not mistaken, and that's in Posavina.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I have already said a few times on the 1st of September, 1992, I stopped being the chief of the public security station in Knezevo. I did some work in the security services centre in Banja Luka, and the unit was called the police brigade of the Banja Luka security services centre, and it was part of some kind of a tactical group or something in the Posavina theatre. I don't recall the name of the Tactical Group. And it was stationed in the village of Obudovac. That's Samac municipality. And it was engaged in combat in Orasje, and I was a member of the command of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. My mistaken entirely. I really do apologise. I lost my focus for a moment. It is a fact that as of the 1st of September, you were in the security services centre. Now, tell me, you say that you were in the command of that unit of the police brigade, but that police brigade had a military commander. Is it not so?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it had a military commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that military commander was called what?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until my arrival, very fortunately, it was Bosko Peulic, and after my arrival Radoslav Djukic, and he was lieutenant-colonel or colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you said "very fortunately for me," I suppose you felt lucky that the commander was not Bosko Peulic in your time.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Could you show us on the map where this unit was and where these -- where these command operations were taking place?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 65 ter 16236.04 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And while we're waiting, you obviously don't have a very good opinion of Mr. Peulic. Is it his qualities as military commander or as a human being that you don't like?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 10236, number 04. It's a map of Bosanski Samac. 00482222 is the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's not a very good map. I'm using it only for it's geography, not to show this ethnic composition that I do not accept. I would just like you to delineate and mark with an X the place where you were stationed. You said Obudovac. It's a bit of a problem that there is writing in yellow, but as far as I can see, it's in the left corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The writing is in black in my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So much the better.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade command was in the centre of Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You held this bit on the right. Can you show us the territory of Orasje municipality where you conducted combat operations?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly the area of responsibility of the brigade was like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could we please put number 1 near Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Number 2 next to the line showing the area of responsibility of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And now if you can tell us where in this area were the HVO, the Croatian Defence Council troops? Mark that with a 3 and a circle.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were on the other side of that line. I misplaced this number 2. The HVO should be on this side, number 3, and number 2 on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The usher will help you delete this wrong marking.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The HVO were on the other side of this red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's it. Now put number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We see this black line above Bosanski Samac. I think it's the Sava River, isn't it? And beyond it is the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mark the Republic of Croatia with 4.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the lower part of the map where was the separation line with the BH Army? If you can.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please put number 5 there.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see Mr. Dobbyn is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. From my understanding of this line of questioning so far, we've been discussing a situation in 1993. Before we go much further, I just wonder if the relevance of this could be explained perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, as I -- as I'm aware that the -- that the -- that the Office of the Prosecutor is going to lead evidence about the deployment of the police brigade of the CSB Banja Luka end of 1992, when the deployment started. Since this witness was actually deployed on the -- on the same location, I thought that it might be worth that we -- that we get the evidence of the witness about the positions when -- at the time when he was there despite the fact that it's the beginning of 1993. It is just for the purposes of cross-examination of witness who is going to testify to this about the -- for the -- for our friends from the Prosecution. In any case, I'm -- I am finished with this line of questioning, and I would like to tender this document if there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the purpose of this is for comparative purposes when the other witness comes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zecevic, could we just have one extra comment on the map. Are we to understand that north of the line where the number 3 is put, that's where the Croatian Army was in control, and south of the other line, which has now disappeared, south of the line which was indicated by 5 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: -- that's where the Bosnian army was in control, and so the -- the police brigade was deployed in the -- in the little area between the Croatian Army and the Bosnian army. Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. And this is also -- I think it will help us understand the situation in -- in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, which is part of our indictment, and this map depicts the municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And this will be Exhibit 1D366, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't have much more, and I'll try to be quick. You testified on the first day that you were one of the founders of the Serbian Democratic Party in Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And as a representative of that party, you were elected into the Assembly and the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were elections into the Municipal Assembly of Knezevo, and that Assembly elected seven of us to represent them in the Autonomous Region of Krajina Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But all this happened before you were appointed chief of the SJB Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you were appointed chief of the SJB, you froze all your political functions in the party and in the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I abandoned them. I didn't freeze them, didn't put them on hold, abandoned them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You did that because it was your legal obligation to do so, in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For that reason, yes, but also because I personally didn't want to be involved in politics any more and wanted to concentrate on my professional work of leading the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the legislation that prevailed stipulated it was incompatible for a chief of the police station to be a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there is this saying that rules are made to be broken, and in this way my successor was also a member of the Assembly at the same time, and his successor in the post of chief of station was also a member of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That seems to indicate that your successors did not abide by the rules and legislation, and they did not care so much for upholding strict professionalism.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't go as far as to say that. I just explained my personal point of view and why I did the things I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You had certain disagreements with the political leadership in the Knezevo municipality, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the Assembly -- sorry, in the municipality there was a National Defence Council before the outbreak of the conflict in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every municipality had a National Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That National Defence Council, just as the committee for national defence in social self-protection, were bodies that were set up in every administrative unit, that is to say municipality, in keeping with the Law on National Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And under this legislation, you were ex officio member of the National Defence Council, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In addition to you, ex officio members were also president of the municipality, president of the Executive Board, the officer for national defence?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody was member of that council ex officio by virtue of the post they held.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After these events in April 1992 and the beginning of the conflict, some people called this body the Crisis Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, it is a fact, isn't it, that regardless of which name you use, the National Defence Council or Crisis Staff, that body, throughout the time you were in Knezevo, the 1st of September, 1992, was made up of the same people and dealt with the same issues. It was basically one and the same body.

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. The separation line, the line separating the territory held by Muslim and Croat forces from the other side was barely one and a half kilometres from the centre of Knezevo, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NENAD KREJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the separation line with the Croatian side, running through the municipality of Knezevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
